extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy / general educated readers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted normative principles and standards from Hobbes' Leviathan concerning origins of religion, the natural condition of mankind, causes of conflict, and the first and second laws of nature (rights, liberty, contracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Four natural seeds of religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion of Ghosts; Ignorance of second causes; Devotion towards what men fear; Taking of things Casuall for Prognostiques — 'in these foure things, Opinion of Ghosts, Ignorance of second causes, Devotion towards what men fear, and Taking of things Casuall for Prognostiques, consisteth the Naturall seed of Religion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes lists these four psychological/original dispositions as the natural basis from which diverse religious ceremonies and beliefs grow; differences in fancy, judgement, and passion cause varied ceremonies that one group may find ridiculous in another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion cultivated for two purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Religion has received culture from two sorts of men: those who 'nourished, and ordered them, according to their own invention' and those who did it 'by Gods commandement, and direction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes distinguishes human/political religion (instituted to secure obedience and civil society) from divine religion (derived from revelation and governing subjects in the kingdom of God); both aim to produce obedience, law, peace, charity, and civil society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion as part of humane politique (political instrument)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Religion of the former sort, is a part of humane Politiques; and teacheth part of the duty which Earthly Kings require of their Subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders and lawmakers among the Gentiles used religion and ceremonies instrumentally to secure obedience and public order; tolerance was allowed so long as the religion did not conflict with civil government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion as divine politique (revealed law)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Religion of the later sort is Divine Politiques; and containeth Precepts to those that have yeelded themselves subjects in the Kingdome of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religions founded by revelation (e.g., Abraham, Moses, Christ) supply duties binding within the 'Kingdome of God' and include law-like precepts beyond mere political expedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs of founders/legislators of religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders and legislators imprinted belief that precepts came from some God or made themselves appear higher than mortals; prescribed ceremonies, sacrifices, and festivals and connected civic prohibitions with divine displeasure so people would obey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes details practical techniques (pretended revelation, priests' authority, ceremonials, consecrated places and revenues) used to induce belief and maintain civil peace; these are described as deliberate political tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracles as necessary testimony of divine calling
rubrics_metrics.description: The testimony that men can render of divine Calling, can be no other, than the operation of Miracles; or true Prophecy, (which also is a Miracle;) or extraordinary Felicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes argues that supernatural signs (miracles, true prophecy, extraordinary fortune) are the only convincing proofs of a divine calling; without such signs later additions claim no more belief than local custom and law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enjoining belief of contradictories undermines credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: That which taketh away the reputation of Wisedome, in him that formeth a Religion, or addeth to it when it is allready formed, is the enjoyning of a beliefe of contradictories: For both parts of a contradiction cannot possibly be true...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demanding belief in contradictions marks ignorance and discredits a religious founder's claimed wisdom; revelation cannot reasonably require belief against natural reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypocrisy/scandal weakens religious sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: That which taketh away the reputation of Sincerity, is the doing, or saying of such things, as appeare to be signes, that what they require other men to believe, is not believed by themselves... all which doings, or sayings are therefore called Scandalous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behaviors like injustice, cruelty, profanity, avarice, and luxury by religious leaders are stumbling blocks that make people reject their religion; pastoral virtue supports faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private ends discredit religious leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: That which taketh away the reputation of Love, is the being detected of private ends: as when the beliefe they require of others, conduceth or seemeth to conduce to the acquiring of Dominion, Riches, Dignity, or secure Pleasure, to themselves onely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If religious prescriptions appear to serve the private advantage of leaders, people will assume self-interest rather than love for others is the motive, thereby undermining belief and obedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion weakened by failure of miracles and pastoral virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Miracles fayling, Faith also failed... the fayling of Vertue in the Pastors, maketh Faith faile in the People.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes uses historical examples (Israel, the Apostles' success vs pagan priests' corruption, Reformation critiques) to argue that lack of miraculous proof and moral failure in clergy cause decline or change in religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Nature (Jus Naturale)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIGHT OF NATURE... is the Liberty each man hath, to use his own power, as he will himselfe, for the preservation of his own Nature; that is to say, of his own Life; and consequently, of doing any thing, which in his own Judgement, and Reason, hee shall conceive to be the aptest means thereunto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes defines the basic natural liberty each person has to preserve life and use means they judge fit; this is foundational for later rules about renouncing rights and forming covenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty defined as absence of external impediments
rubrics_metrics.description: By LIBERTY, is understood... the absence of externall Impediments: which Impediments, may oft take away part of a mans power to do what hee would; but cannot hinder him from using the power left him...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that liberty is not unlimited power but absence of external constraints; liberty can be partially impeded yet still permit exercise of remaining power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of Nature (Lex Naturalis)
rubrics_metrics.description: A LAW OF NATURE, (Lex Naturalis,) is a Precept, or generall Rule, found out by Reason, by which a man is forbidden to do, that, which is destructive of his life, or taketh away the means of preserving the same; and to omit, that, by which he thinketh it may be best preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes distinguishes Right (liberty to act) from Law (obligation to act or forbear) and positions laws of nature as rational rules for self-preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: First (Fundamental) Law of Nature: seek peace and follow it
rubrics_metrics.description: The first branch... containeth the first, and Fundamentall Law of Nature; which is, 'To seek Peace, and follow it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes elevates pursuit of peace as the primary rational rule for self-preservation; when peace cannot be obtained, defending oneself by all means is permitted (second branch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Law of Nature: mutual renunciation of rights for peace
rubrics_metrics.description: From this Fundamentall Law of Nature... is derived this second Law; 'That a man be willing, when others are so too... to lay down this right to all things; and be contented with so much liberty against other men, as he would allow other men against himselfe.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the reciprocity principle (Golden Rule) applied to covenant-making: mutual limitation of natural rights is required to end the state of war and secure peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: What it is to lay down a right
rubrics_metrics.description: To Lay Downe a mans Right to any thing, is to Devest himselfe of the Liberty, of hindring another of the benefit of his own Right to the same... the effect... is but so much diminution of impediments to the use of his own Right originall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes explains that renouncing a right doesn't grant new rights to others but removes obstacles so each can enjoy original rights without mutual interference; this is the basis of obligation and justice in covenants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renouncing or transferring rights creates obligation (duty/justice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Right is layd aside, either by simply Renouncing it; or by Transferring it to another... And when a man hath in either manner abandoned, or granted away his Right; then is he said to be OBLIGED, or BOUND... and that such hindrance is INJUSTICE, and INJURY, as being Sine Jure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes sets out how voluntary renunciation or transfer (by words or actions) binds the renouncer not to frustrate the granted benefit; undoing such voluntary acts counts as injustice—paralleling contractual/consensual obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three principal causes of quarrel
rubrics_metrics.description: In the nature of man, we find three principall causes of quarrel. First, Competition; Secondly, Diffidence; Thirdly, Glory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each cause is tied to common human motivations: competition for gain, diffidence for safety (anticipation), and glory for reputation; these explain why conflict arises absent a common power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of war as a state of known disposition to fight
rubrics_metrics.description: WARRE, consisteth not in Battell onely, or the act of fighting; but in a tract of time, wherein the Will to contend by Battell is sufficiently known... the nature of War, consisteth not in actuall fighting; but in the known disposition thereto, during all the time there is no assurance to the contrary. All other time is PEACE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes emphasizes temporal and dispositional aspects of war (continuous insecurity) rather than isolated acts of fighting; peace is the absence of that disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of the state of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: In such condition, there is no place for Industry... no Culture of the Earth; no Navigation... no Knowledge of the face of the Earth; no Arts; no Letters; no Society; and... continuall feare, and danger of violent death; And the life of man, solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a normative justification for forming common power/society: absence of security eliminates productive, cultural, and social activity.
